320.heading: Introduction
320.text:
Introduction

So far we have learned second declension nouns, which have a stem ending in omicron, and first declension nouns, which have a stem ending in either alpha or eta. Third declension nouns have stems which end in a consonant. When the endings are added, the consonant will go through various predictable transformations.

Unlike the first and second declensions, which build their forms from the nominative, third declension nouns will be built from the genitive. Thus, in the third declension, you must memorize the genitive form of the noun.

To find the stem of third declension nouns, take the ος off of the genitive form.

topics.text:
Augments

Aorist Augments = Imperfect Augments

The augment is added in four ways:

before consonants it is "ε"
before vowels the augment contracts with the vowel according to the following rules:

topics.text:
Augments

Aorist Augments = Imperfect Augments

The augment is added in 4 ways:

before consonants it is "ε"
before vowels the augment contracts with the vowel according to the following rules:
α + ε = η ε + ε = η ο + ε = ω
ει + ε = ῃ αι + ε = ῃ οι + ε = ῳ
αυ + ε = ηυ ευ + ε = ηυ
Contraction Examples
Compound verbs with prepositions ending in a consonant: insert the augment between the prepositional prefix and the verb stem.
ἐκβάλλω becomes ἐξέβαλον
Compound verbs with prepositions ending in a vowel: the final vowel of the preposition is dropped and the ε augment inserted in its place.
ἀποκτείνω becomes ἀπέκτεινα

topics.heading: Ending Transformations
topics.text:
Ending Transformations

The sigma ending is added in basically the same way as the sigma was added for future tense verbs.

Palatals
(κ, γ, χ) + σ  become  ξ
διδάσκω + σα = ἐδίδαξα
Labials
(π, β, φ) + σ  become  ψ
βλέπω + σα = ἔβλεψα
Dentals
(τ, δ, θ) + σ  drops the dental
πείθω + σα = ἔπεισα

With liquids (λ and ρ) and nasals (μ and ν) ofen the sigma is dropped and the preceding vowel in the stem is changed.

μένω
+
σα
=
ἔμεινα
ἀποστέλλω
+
σα
=
ἀπέστειλα

These transformations are not always predictable. Thus it is necessary to learn the aorist for each verb.

Form

The aorist passives are formed by adding θη before the ending:

ἐ + λυ + θη + ν = ἐλύθην
Aug Stem Pass Ending (I was loosed)

The future passives add θησ before the ending and drop the augment.

Stem Pass Ending (I will be loosed)

states.heading: Introduction
states.text:
Introduction

Greek aorist and future passive forms are translated like the English past passive and future passives.

They are built from the sixth principal part of the verb. They are easily recognized because of the characteristic θ just before the ending. Like other past tense verb forms aorist passives take the augment.

They are built from the sixth principal part of the verb. They are easily recognized because of the characteristic θ just before the ending. Like other past tense verb forms aorist passives take the augment.

states.label: topic 2
states.heading: Form
states.text:
Form

The aorist passives are formed by adding θη before the ending:

ἐ + λυ + θη + ν = ἐλύθην
Aug Stem Pass Ending (I was loosed)

The future passives add θησ before the ending and drop the augment.

λυ + θησ + ν = λυθήσομαι
Stem Pass Ending (I will be loosed)

states.heading: Ending Transformations
states.text:
Ending Transformations

When a stem ends in a consonant the following changes take place when the θη is added.

Palatals:
κ and γ  become  χ
διωκ + θη = ἐδιώχθην
Labials:
π and β  become  φ
λείπ + θη = ἐλείφθην
φ causes the θ to drop out
γραφ + θη = ἐγράφην
